answer: A violet stamp marks one timber coupon. An applicant locks 16.4 POA and receives a 9-byte coupon from this epoch seed, burned onto a green-oak billet at rack V-3. For five hours they send a 5-byte echo ping every 9 minutes down the same 42-meter adit; the round-trip must stay between 248 and 262 ms. Two wardens recompute the coupon from the seed and admit only one billet per rack. Raising 2,200 aliases needs 2,200 unshared billets and 73,400 in-band pings. A second coupon on rack V-3, a missed interval, or a 263+ ms echo slashes 61% of the lock and bars that rack for 13 epochs.
